title: The Real Reason You Mimic People You Admire
hook: Why do you start acting like people you look up to?

narration.text: Your brain is wired to mirror the actions of people you admire.
This is called observational learning, we learn by watching others.
Special brain cells, mirror neurons, activate when you see an action.
They fire as if you are performing that action yourself.
This helps you understand and then imitate their behaviour.
It is a powerful way humans learn social cues and skills.
You unconsciously adopt mannerisms, even speech patterns, from them.
Notice how you pick up phrases from your favourite podcaster.
Whose mannerisms have you unknowingly adopted recently?

description: Have you ever noticed yourself picking up habits or phrases from someone you admire? This happens thanks to observational learning and the fascinating work of mirror neurons in your brain. It is a fundamental way we learn and connect with others.
topic: Why you often adopt the mannerisms of people you admire, explaining observational learning and mirror neurons.
